answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut and 14-day renewal deadline create extreme time pressure. Switching vendors (memory_c2) achieved cost cuts but risks delivery disruption given the 94% line utilization with no buffer. Deferring (memory_c5) is impossible given the hard contract expiration. Renewing without negotiation wastes leverage. Adding second source (memory_c3) addresses risk but doesn't solve the 18% mandate directly. Negotiation offers the highest probability of meeting the cost target while preserving incumbent stability and delivery reliability. Memory_c4 demonstrated that benchmarking-driven renegotiation recovered real margin; memory_c6 showed multi-year terms unlock volume pricing; memory_c2 proved switching is operationally feasible but carries execution risk we cannot afford at 94% utilization. Verifying memory_c4 will confirm the benchmarking methodology and margin recovery magnitude to ground the negotiation strategy. A standard experiment scope allows testing new terms on partial volume first, preserving incumbent relationship while reducing commitment risk if 18% target proves unachievable.
